req.title: Create new post
req.statement: The system shall insert a new post attributed to the logged-in user when POST /create receives a title and body, then redirect to /.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that POST /create must insert a new post attributed to the logged-in user and redirect to /. I design: (1) a positive EP test confirming 302 redirect and DB row insertion with correct author_id; (2) a negative NEG test confirming unauthenticated access redirects to login (not /create); (3) a boundary BVA test with minimum-length title ('A') and body ('A') confirming acceptance; (4) a negative DT test confirming empty title is rejected and no row inserted; (5) a state-transition STC test confirming the post count increments by exactly 1 after creation; (6) a boundary BVA test with maximum-length title (120 chars) and body (1000 chars) confirming acceptance. All tests use exact-value assertions to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_create_post_happy_path_redirects_and_inserts_row
preconditions: User is logged in via POST /auth/login
actions: POST /create with title='Test Post Title' and body='Test post body content'
expected: Exactly one new post row exists in DB with title='Test Post Title' and author_id=1
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

def test_create_post_happy_path_redirects_and_inserts_row():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    r = client.post('/create', data={'title': 'Test Post Title', 'body': 'Test post body content'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'
    with app.app_context():
        db = get_db()
        row = db.execute("SELECT * FROM post WHERE title = 'Test Post Title'").fetchone()
        assert row is not None
        assert row['title'] == 'Test Post Title'
        assert row['body'] == 'Test post body content'
        assert row['author_id'] == 1

test_create_post_happy_path_redirects_and_inserts_row()

actions: POST /create with title='Some Title' and body='Some body' without logging in
expected: No new post row inserted in DB
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

def test_create_post_unauthenticated_redirects_to_login():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    with app.app_context():
        count_before = db = get_db()
        count_before = db.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM post').fetchone()[0]
    r = client.post('/create', data={'title': 'Some Title', 'body': 'Some body'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'
    with app.app_context():
        count_after = get_db().execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM post').fetchone()[0]
        assert count_after == count_before

tests.name: test_create_post_maximum_length_title_and_body_accepted
preconditions: User Diya (id=4, password=cloud) is logged in
actions: POST /create with title of exactly 120 'X' chars and body of exactly 1000 'X' chars
expected: New post row with 120-char title and 1000-char body and author_id=4 inserted
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

def test_create_post_maximum_length_title_and_body_accepted():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Diya', 'password': 'cloud'})
    long_title = 'X' * 120
    long_body = 'X' * 1000
    r = client.post('/create', data={'title': long_title, 'body': long_body})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'
    with app.app_context():
        row = get_db().execute('SELECT * FROM post WHERE title = ?', (long_title,)).fetchone()
        assert row is not None
        assert row['title'] == long_title
        assert len(row['title']) == 120
        assert row['body'] == long_body
        assert len(row['body']) == 1000
        assert row['author_id'] == 4

test_create_post_maximum_length_title_and_body_accepted()
